title: Sarawak Energy Marathon 2026: a 1am start, an AIMS-certified course, and every ringgit to charity
seo_title: Sarawak Energy Marathon 2026: Course, Fees and Entry Guide
meta_description: The 11th Sarawak Energy Marathon runs 9 August 2026 in Kuching, with a 1am marathon flag-off, AIMS-certified routes and all entry fees going to charity. Entry closed 30 June 2026.
dek: Kuching's flagship road race has grown from a corporate fun run into an AIMS-accredited marathon with a RM201,500 prize purse -- and it still gives away every sen of entry revenue.
verdict: This is one of the better-value marathons in Southeast Asia, and unusually, that is not an accident of a weak currency: Sarawak Energy channels 100% of registration fees to charity and funds the race itself [2][4]. You get an AIMS-certified course [3], a RM201,500 prize purse [2] and a genuinely international field [2] for an early-bird entry of RM90. The catch for 2026 is timing -- entry closed on 30 June [4][5], so if you are reading this before race day on 9 August, treat it as a scouting report for 2027 rather than something you can still enter. The other catch is the 1am marathon flag-off [1], which is a real and deliberate concession to Kuching's heat, not a gimmick.

sections.heading: From corporate fun run to AIMS-certified marathon
paragraphs: The 2026 event is the 11th edition. It began in 2013 as the Sarawak Energy Isthmus Run, a shorter-distance community race built around the Kuching Isthmus, and was rebranded to the Sarawak Energy Marathon for its 10th edition in 2025 [4].

That rebrand was substantive rather than cosmetic. The 2025 edition introduced the full 42.195km distance for the first time and secured international accreditation in the same year [6]. The race now holds full member status with the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races, and all four of its routes are certified [3].

For a runner, AIMS certification is the difference between a measured course and an approximate one. If you are chasing a time that you want to stand up -- a personal best, a qualifying attempt, a club record -- it matters that the distance is what the race says it is.

sections.heading: The course: a night lap of Kuching's landmarks
paragraphs: The marathon flags off at 1:00am from Menara Sarawak Energy, with the half marathon at 4:00am, the 10km at 5:45am and the 5km at 6:15am [1]. The staggered start times are all built around the same constraint: Kuching sits barely above one degree north of the equator, and a daytime marathon there would be a survival exercise rather than a race.

The route runs through the Kuching Isthmus and past a dense run of the city's landmarks -- the Darul Hana Bridge, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly Building, the Borneo Cultures Museum, the Kuching cat statue and the Kuching Waterfront [2]. Runners also pass the Juma'ani Bridge and the Satria Pertiwi Complex.

One practical consequence of the 1am start that the official material does not spell out: you will run most of the marathon in darkness and see comparatively little of the scenery the route is designed around. The landmarks are lit, but if the sightseeing is the draw, the 10km or 5km with their post-dawn starts deliver more of it.
AIMS lists no course profile and directs runners to the race website for the route map [3], so if you need elevation detail you will have to source it from the organiser directly.

sections.heading: What it costs, and where the money goes
paragraphs: Entry is tiered by how early you commit. The full marathon runs RM90 early bird, RM120 normal and RM140 late; the half marathon RM70 / RM100 / RM120; the 10km RM60 / RM80 / RM100; and the 5km RM40 / RM60 / RM80 [1].

Even at the late-entry rate, RM140 for an AIMS-certified marathon is low by regional standards. The reason is structural: Sarawak Energy underwrites the event and directs all registration fees to charitable organisations across Sarawak [2][4]. You are not buying a race entry so much as making a donation that comes with a bib.

Age minimums apply and vary by distance -- 18 for the full marathon, 16 for the half, 15 for the 10km, and none for the 5km fun run [1]. Veteran categories open at 45 for the longer distances, and the full marathon carries a separate Malaysian National category alongside the Open [1].

sections.heading: The field and the prize money
paragraphs: More than 5,700 runners had registered when the organiser last reported numbers, against roughly 6,000 for the 2025 edition, with the organiser projecting around 7,000 by the deadline [2][4]. Close to 500 of those entered the full marathon [2] -- a reminder that this is still a race whose centre of gravity is the shorter distances.

The 2026 prize purse is RM201,500, up from RM185,000 in 2025, with RM15,000 each for the men's and women's Open full marathon winners [2]. Prize money at that level does real work in attracting a competitive front end, and the entry list reflects it: runners from Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia, Kenya, the Netherlands, Singapore, France, the United Kingdom and the United States [2].
The Kenyan entries in particular are the signal worth reading. East African elites follow prize money, and their presence is a reasonable proxy for whether a regional marathon's purse is serious.

sections.heading: Entry for 2026 has closed
paragraphs: Registration for the 2026 edition closed on 30 June 2026 [4][5]. There is no indication of a late or on-the-day entry window.

This is worth stating plainly because aggregator listings for this race can lag badly behind the organiser, and several still describe entry as open well after the deadline passed. If you find a page offering 2026 entry now, check the date on it before you trust it.

The race has been held in the second week of August every year [3], so a 2027 edition in the same window is a reasonable planning assumption -- but treat it as an assumption until the organiser confirms it.

sections.heading: Who it suits
paragraphs: It suits a runner who wants a legitimate, accurately measured marathon without a European or Japanese entry fee, and who is comfortable with heat, humidity and a start time that wrecks a night's sleep. It suits a first-time marathoner less well than the price tag suggests -- an overnight start is a hard thing to pace if you have never done it.
It also suits anyone who wants their entry fee to do something. The 100%-to-charity model is rare enough at this scale that it is a genuine differentiator rather than marketing.
It suits you poorly if you want a scenic race. The route passes some of the best-looking civic architecture in Borneo, and for the marathon you will experience nearly all of it in the dark.

faqs.question: Can I still register for the Sarawak Energy Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: No. Registration for the 2026 edition closed on 30 June 2026, and the organiser has not announced a late or race-day entry window. The race itself is held on 9 August 2026 in Kuching. Runners interested in taking part should watch for the 2027 edition instead.

faqs.question: What time does the Sarawak Energy Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Start times are staggered by distance. The full marathon flags off at 1:00am, the half marathon at 4:00am, the 10km at 5:45am and the 5km fun run at 6:15am. The overnight starts exist to keep runners out of Kuching's equatorial daytime heat and humidity.

faqs.question: How much does the Sarawak Energy Marathon cost to enter?
faqs.answer: Fees are tiered by how early you register. The full marathon costs RM90 early bird, RM120 normal and RM140 late entry. The half marathon runs RM70 to RM120, the 10km RM60 to RM100, and the 5km RM40 to RM80. All fees go to Sarawak charities.

faqs.question: Is the Sarawak Energy Marathon course certified?
faqs.answer: Yes. The race holds full member status with the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races, and all four of its routes are AIMS-certified. Certification was first secured for the 2025 edition, the same year the full 42.195km marathon distance was introduced to the event.

faqs.question: Where does the Sarawak Energy Marathon route go?
faqs.answer: The course starts at Menara Sarawak Energy and runs through the Kuching Isthmus, passing the Darul Hana Bridge, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly Building, the Borneo Cultures Museum, the Kuching cat statue and the Kuching Waterfront, along with the Juma'ani Bridge and Satria Pertiwi Complex.

editorial_notes: Written 2026-08-05 against primary sources, each fact traced to the numbered citation beside it. No pull quotes are included because no source carries a verbatim on-record quote from a named official. No rating is given: the 2026 edition had not been run at the time of writing and no participant feedback exists to score. Note that the entity record for this race carried registration_status 'open' when this was written, which contradicts the 30 June deadline reported by two independent sources; the entity has been corrected.
